eyebrow: Quantum Programming with Q# & Azure Quantum · Chapter 3
subtitle: Lesson 14 · Azure Quantum Workspace & Resource Estimation

caption: Every job moves through the same states: Waiting, Executing, then Succeeded or Failed — regardless of which target you submitted to.

eyebrow: Submit, poll, fetch — from the CLI
code:
az quantum job submit --resource-group rg-quantum-dev \
  --workspace-name qsharp-dev-workspace \
  --target-id ionq.simulator \
  --project path/to/project --job-name my-first-job

az quantum job show --resource-group rg-quantum-dev \
  --workspace-name qsharp-dev-workspace --job-id <job-id>

az quantum job output --resource-group rg-quantum-dev \
  --workspace-name qsharp-dev-workspace --job-id <job-id>
caption: job submit returns a job ID immediately; job show reports status; job output retrieves results once Succeeded.

code:
job = workspace.submit(program, target="ionq.simulator", shots=1000, job_name="my-first-job")
job.wait_until_completed()   # blocks, polling status internally
results = job.get_results()  # histogram of measurement outcomes, once Succeeded
caption: wait_until_completed() is exactly the polling loop you'd otherwise write by hand with repeated job-show calls.
